shelters.name: Arizona Humane Society
shelters.description: Arizona's largest animal welfare organization, operating the state's largest trauma hospital for homeless animals. Dedicated to saving vulnerable pets through innovative medical programs, emergency rescue, and comprehensive adoption services.

shelters.name: Arizona Animal Welfare League & SPCA
shelters.description: The oldest and largest no-kill shelter in Arizona, founded in 1971. Merged with Arizona SPCA in 2007. Rescues, rehabilitates, and rehomes more than 4,000 dogs and cats annually.

shelters.name: Maricopa County Animal Care and Control - West
shelters.description: One of the nation's largest open-admission shelters, serving the animals and people of Maricopa County with adoption services, vaccinations, spay/neuter, and licensing. Maintains 95% save rate.

shelters.name: Maricopa County Animal Care and Control - East
shelters.description: New 84,000 sq ft East Valley Animal Care Center opened May 2024 with 346 kennels. Serving Mesa and East Valley communities.

shelters.name: Pima Animal Care Center
shelters.description: The community's only open-admission shelter with the largest selection of adoptable dogs, cats, puppies, and kittens. All adopted pets are microchipped, spayed/neutered, and vaccinated.

shelters.name: Friends of Pima Animal Care Center
shelters.description: Nonprofit partner to Pima Animal Care Center, providing resources to support neglected, abandoned, and abused pets. Named Best Non-Profit in Arizona Daily Star Readers' Choice Awards six consecutive years.

shelters.name: Humane Society of Southern Arizona
shelters.description: Independent local nonprofit established in 1944, dedicated to sheltering and placement of animals, prevention of cruelty, and education on humane treatment. Offers low-cost spay/neuter and TNR programs.

shelters.name: HALO Animal Rescue
shelters.description: Founded in 1994, HALO provides a safe haven for thousands of homeless dogs and cats annually. Never euthanizes for space and ensures every pet receives full veterinary support before adoption.

shelters.name: Lost Our Home Pet Rescue
shelters.description: No-kill rescue dedicated to bridging the care gap between people in crisis and pets who have no place to go. Over 12,000 pets adopted into loving homes.

shelters.name: Foothills Animal Rescue
shelters.description: Non-profit founded in 1995, operating an adoption-guarantee facility where dogs and cats remain in care until finding loving homes. Award-winning Brynne Smith Memorial Campus.

shelters.name: Sun Cities 4 Paws Rescue
shelters.description: No-kill cat-only animal rescue and shelter serving the Sun Cities area with adoption services.

shelters.name: Yavapai Humane Society
shelters.description: Private non-profit providing animal care for stray dogs and cats in Prescott, Prescott Valley, and Yavapai County.

shelters.name: United Animal Friends
shelters.description: Volunteer-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2003. Operates Snip n' Go Clinic providing affordable spay/neuter services.

shelters.name: Verde Valley Humane Society
shelters.description: Provides shelter and care for homeless animals throughout Cottonwood, Verde Valley, Yavapai County. Took in 756 homeless pets in 2024.

shelters.name: Humane Society of Central Arizona
shelters.description: Animal shelter providing adoption services for dogs and cats in the Payson and central Arizona area. Offers Senior to Senior program.

shelters.name: Coconino Humane Association

shelters.name: High Country Humane

shelters.name: Humane Society of Sedona

notes: Exhaustive collection of Arizona animal shelters, humane societies, rescue organizations, wildlife rehabilitators, farm sanctuaries, and senior pet sanctuaries. Major organizations include Arizona Humane Society (state's largest), AAWL & SPCA (oldest/largest no-kill since 1971), Maricopa County ACC (one of nation's largest open-admission with 95% save rate), and Phoenix Herpetological Sanctuary (largest reptile sanctuary in US). Coverage spans Phoenix metro, Tucson, Prescott, Flagstaff, Sedona, Lake Havasu City, Yuma, and rural areas. Includes breed-specific rescues (Chihuahua, Pitbull, Labrador, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd, Doberman, Mastiff), wildlife rehabilitation, horse rescues, farm sanctuaries, and senior dog sanctuaries.
